thread:
mileena: CI run hit the wrong project after a key rotation. We set REDWOOD_PROJECT=exp-run but requests went to exp-prod.

ryan: did the SDK log anything about precedence?

mileena: yes: "Using project from token: exp-prod (token scope)". We expected env to override.

tara: SDK doc used to say env overrides token scope. Maybe a change slipped in.

mileena: also, when we rotated the API key in the same job, the running service kept using the old key for ~60s and then started 401ing.

ryan: two bugs: silent precedence change and no runtime reload for rotated creds.

tara: proposed fixes: 1) make precedence explicit and deterministic: constructor > CLI flags > REDWOOD_PROJECT env > token fallback; surface a startup warning if env and token disagree. 2) provide client.reloadCredentials() and a small local socket the CLI can hit to notify processes to reload.

mileena: sounds good. Could we also add a strict CI mode that fails on mismatch (REDWOOD_PROJECT_STRICT=true)? That would have caught this earlier.

ryan: +1. And default logging at info level should show source of project (env or token) so users see what's being used.

tara: I'll take the SDK patch: add precedence, warning, reload API, and tests. ETA 48h.

auth-bot: created issue RW-SDK-321: "clarify env/token precedence + rotation reload API" assigned to tara.

mileena: thanks. Also adding a lint step in our sampleapp CI to catch REDWOOD_PROJECT vs token mismatches.

ryan: once PR is ready, let's add a short note to quickstart: prefer passing --project in CI or using per-job scoped tokens.

tara: will include docs and migration note in changelog.
